key_insight: Storage conditions measurably alter the magnetic and thermoelectric signatures of rutile flux-cored welding wires, enabling non-destructive assessment of degradation risk.
engineering_relevance: These results suggest a practical quality-control path for deciding whether stored consumables remain suitable for industrial welding use.
method: Stored wires in four environments for 3, 6, and 12 months
Measured Seebeck coefficient and bulk magnetic properties, including Magnetic Barkhausen Noise
Compared parameter changes with visual inspection and statistical correlation analysis
evidence_signal: Visual checks showed acceptable surface condition, while MBN amplitude, MBN envelope area, and thermoelectric response changed with time and environment, with correlations above 0.9 in some cases.
watch_item: The approach is promising, but field implementation will need calibration for environment-specific effects and validation across wire types and storage conditions.
paper_title: Feasibility study of using magnetic and thermoelectric methods for the assessment of storage-induced changes in flux-cored welding wires
